Moore is the short complement (16 targets, 80 air yards, 105 yards). script.flip1: Chicago hangs around or leads. pre_mortem: It is the morning after and the Croskey-Merritt over lost because Sam Cosmi did not play, the Washington interior got no movement, and Jacory finished around 9 carries for 35 yards while Chris Rodriguez stole the short-yardage work. The 111-yard game was one long run against a defense that, even at 6.15 yards per carry allowed, was not gashed between the tackles once the starting guard sat. The Odunze over lost on the same night if Washington rolled the coverage his way and Chicago's 22 implied points came on a short touchdown to Kmet plus field goals: 5 catches for 48 yards, with the 128-yard week left behind as the outlier and the 62-yard week as the real template. Wind that was never saved in the pack is the other silent killer for a 375-air-yard receiver outdoors at night in Washington. If Chicago instead led early, Croskey-Merritt was the leg that had to die and Odunze was the one that should have cashed; a split would mean the base script was wrong, not that the two legs needed opposite games.
slip_story: One base-script story for a 27.5 to 22.0 game: Washington leads and runs late, Chicago throws as the dog in a 49.5 total. Croskey-Merritt rush yards over is the favorite clock stack. Odunze receiving yards over is the dog pass stack. They can win together without a shootout and without a blowout. Do not add a total under, a Swift rush over, a Deebo or McCaffrey over, or any touchdown. Two legs, one market per player, no depth-receiver add. Flip 1 (Chicago leads) is the shared failure mode for the rush leg only; the slip is still one story, not two scripts mixed.
